clue.text: Shakespeare's first rude mechanical deprived of a limited opportunity

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Shakespeare's is wanted
rude here means rough and unpolished, so the letters left are knocked into a new shape
deprived of says the clue's a is taken away from the fodder word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bottom and his fellow rude mechanicals of A Midsummer Night's Dream stand little chance of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rude mechanical' points to Shakespeare's amateur actors, but 'rude' is the anagram signal. 'Deprived of a' leaves MECHANICL, which 'rude' rearranges after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a slender likelihood of something happening is an opportunity with very limited prospects.

clue.text: Mini maybe losing top end of revs giving you a funny turn

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter drops out of the garment

parts.note: a mini is a short type of skirt; maybe marks it as an example

indicators.note: the top end of a word in a down light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Mini car over-revving gives its driver an alarming moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mini' wants to be the car, with revs as engine speed; it is a short skirt. 'Losing top end of revs' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch is a funny turn, a turn being a performer's act on stage.

clue.text: Oval the venue for this sport

definitions.text: Oval the venue for this sport

parts.words: Oval the venue for this sport
parts.note: the Oval suggests the London cricket ground, but the sport here is the American open-wheel racing raced chiefly on oval speedways

explanation.surface: The Oval is where this game is played.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a famous London cricket ground, so cricket is the obvious first thought; the four letters lead instead to American motor racing on oval circuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy car racing, named after Indianapolis, is run largely on oval tracks, so an oval is its venue.

clue.text: Lay water supply for one in public sector

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb about putting pipes down; it is the adjective meaning non-religious.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of government employees running state administration forms the core of the public sector.

clue.text: A navy vessel? You bet!

parts.note: a dhow is an Arab sailing vessel

clue.text: Climbs will get hard for late starter making room for judgment

indicators.note: will get ... for says one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: clambers means climbs awkwardly

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A latecomer scrambles in to find a room where a judgment is being given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will get hard for late starter' replaces the L of CLAMBERS (the first letter of 'late') with H.

clue.text: Bar Suggs being almost half-cut, Madness' hard core is entertained

indicators.note: is entertained says one piece is taken in by the other as a guest
half of a five-letter name cut away, near enough, leaves its first three letters
the hard core of a word is its very centre letter

explanation.surface: Suggs, lead singer of the band Madness, half-drunk in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Suggs fronts the British ska band Madness. 'Almost half-cut' leaves SUG; the core of MADNESS is N, taken in by 'is entertained'. Snug is also one of Shakespeare's rude mechanicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cosy private room in a British pub is a bar of this kind.

clue.text: Computer buffs, according to Spooner, are not early-to-bed types?

parts.note: a byte is a computer unit of data, giving the sound 'bite'
nerds are enthusiasts, buffs

explanation.surface: Computer enthusiasts are known for staying up late.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'byte nerds' gives 'nite birds'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who stay up and go out late at night are owls, the opposite of early-to-bed sorts.

clue.text: Gourmet banker from Basel perhaps devouring fancy roast

explanation.surface: A Swiss banker who loves good food tucks into an elaborate roast.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of fine food and drink is a gourmet; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Popular dope — one may take double or single

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
div is slang for an idiot, a dope

dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: A popular drug, taken in a double or single dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs; it is a fool. DIV is British slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something separate and on its own, for one person, is single: the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Lamb cooked in cheese not a learner's preservation process

clue.text: Cruelly erased Des's from names on Christmas card list?

clue.text: Production of intro to Chris Rea disc is in the can

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: A sparse, essentially loveless Dvorak composition — hence his long face?

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the middle letters are taken
a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh
love is zero in tennis, so the round letter is removed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes AR from SPARSE; 'loveless' removes O from DVORAK; 'composition' rearranges ARDVRAK.
explanation.definitionFit: The African anteater has a long snout, so a long face is its trademark, playfully read as a glum look.
